Also known as paintless dent removal or PDR, it offers an alternative to fillers and repainting when the damage qualifies. | How does PDR work? | Technicians use specialized tools, lighting and controlled pressure to gradually reshape damaged metal. Depending on the dent and access, tools may work from behind the panel or use appropriate pulling techniques from the outside. | The aim is to restore the panel’s shape while keeping the existing finish. This takes careful assessment and precise work; the right approach depends on the individual dent. | Which dents can be repaired? | Door dings, some creases, larger dents and hail damage may be candidates. Intact paint, manageable metal stretching and suitable panel access generally make a repair more feasible. | Cracked paint, prior refinishing, sharp damage or excessive stretching may limit results or require conventional body repair. Photos help with an initial assessment, but an in-person inspection may be necessary. | Why preserve the original finish? | For a suitable PDR repair, there is no need to repaint the panel or add body filler. Show us the panel and our technicians will help you understand your options. | Get a free estimate ↗ | Call (321) 407-9700 | What is paintless dent repair? | Paintless dent repair, or PDR, uses specialized tools and controlled pressure to reshape suitable dented vehicle panels while preserving the existing paint. Paint condition, metal stretching and access determine whether it is a good option. | Can you fix my dent without repainting? | Possibly. Our technicians consider the dent’s depth and shape, the condition of the finish, previous repairs and panel access. Cracked paint, severe stretching or sharp damage may require a different approach. Send photos for an initial assessment. | Do you come to my home or workplace? | Yes. Orlando Dent Company provides mobile service in Orlando and nearby communities, including Winter Park, Winter Garden, Windermere, Lake Nona, Ocoee, Kissimmee and other surrounding areas. Our technicians will discuss a suitable work area, vehicle access and weather conditions when arranging your appointment. | How much does dent repair cost? | Estimates are free. Pricing depends on the size, depth, location and number of dents, panel material, access and any trim removal needed. Our technicians review your photos and confirm the repair details after inspecting the vehicle. There is no single price that fits every dent. | What photos should I send for an estimate? | Send a wider photo showing the affected panel, a close-up and an angled photo that makes the dent visible. Reflections can help reveal its shape. Include your vehicle’s year, make, model and your city. The online form accepts JPG, PNG and WebP photos, with no videos. Please keep personal documents out of the pictures. | How long will the repair take? | Timing varies with the damage and access needed. An accessible door ding can require much less time than a complex crease or multiple hail dents. Our technicians will discuss the expected repair time when they assess your vehicle. | Can PDR damage the paint? | PDR is intended to preserve the existing finish. Weakened paint, previous refinishing and sharp or deep damage can increase the risk of cracking or lifting. Our technicians check the area and discuss relevant limitations before work begins. | Do you repair hail damage and larger dents? | Yes, subject to assessment. Hail dents, larger dents and creases may qualify for PDR. Metal stretching, paint condition and panel access influence what can be achieved. Photos help our technicians decide the next step. | What if the dent also has a scratch? | A dent repair does not automatically repair damaged paint. Light surface marks and paint transfer are different from scratches through the finish. Our technicians can inspect the area and explain whether the dent is suitable for PDR or whether paintwork or another service is needed. | Can you work with an insurance claim? | Yes, please let us know if you plan to use insurance. Your insurer determines coverage, deductibles and claim requirements. subpages.text_content: What Is Paintless Dent Repair? | Orlando Dent Company | Skip to content | MOBILE DENT REPAIR · ORLANDO & SURROUNDING AREAS | Talk directly to our technicians (321) 407-9700 | Menu | Home | Services | Our work | About us | FAQs | Free estimate ↗ | Call ODC: (321) 407-9700 | UNDERSTAND YOUR OPTIONS. | What is | paintless dent repair? | A way to reshape suitable dented vehicle panels while preserving the existing paint. Also known as paintless dent removal or PDR, it offers an alternative to fillers and repainting when the damage qualifies. | How does PDR work? | Technicians use specialized tools, lighting and controlled pressure to gradually reshape damaged metal. Depending on the dent and access, tools may work from behind the panel or use appropriate pulling techniques from the outside. | The aim is to restore the panel’s shape while keeping the existing finish. This takes careful assessment and precise work; the right approach depends on the individual dent. | Which dents can be repaired? | Door dings, some creases, larger dents and hail damage may be candidates. Intact paint, manageable metal stretching and suitable panel access generally make a repair more feasible. | Cracked paint, prior refinishing, sharp damage or excessive stretching may limit results or require conventional body repair. Photos help with an initial assessment, but an in-person inspection may be necessary. | Why preserve the original finish? | For a suitable PDR repair, there is no need to repaint the panel or add body filler. That avoids color matching and paint overspray associated with refinishing and helps retain the vehicle’s original finish. | What affects cost and repair time? | The number, size, depth and location of dents matter, along with panel material, access, trim removal and previous repairs. Show us the panel and our technicians will help you understand your options. | Get a free estimate ↗ | Call (321) 407-9700 | What is paintless dent repair? | Paintless dent repair, or PDR, uses specialized tools and controlled pressure to reshape suitable dented vehicle panels while preserving the existing paint. Paint condition, metal stretching and access determine whether it is a good option. | Can you fix my dent without repainting? | Possibly. Our technicians consider the dent’s depth and shape, the condition of the finish, previous repairs and panel access. Cracked paint, severe stretching or sharp damage may require a different approach. Send photos for an initial assessment. | Do you come to my home or workplace? | Yes. Orlando Dent Company provides mobile service in Orlando and nearby communities, including Winter Park, Winter Garden, Windermere, Lake Nona, Ocoee, Kissimmee and other surrounding areas. Our technicians will discuss a suitable work area, vehicle access and weather conditions when arranging your appointment. | How much does dent repair cost? | Estimates are free. Pricing depends on the size, depth, location and number of dents, panel material, access and any trim removal needed. Our technicians review your photos and confirm the repair details after inspecting the vehicle. There is no single price that fits every dent. | What photos should I send for an estimate? | Send a wider photo showing the affected panel, a close-up and an angled photo that makes the dent visible. Reflections can help reveal its shape. Include your vehicle’s year, make, model and your city. The online form accepts JPG, PNG and WebP photos, with no videos. Please keep personal documents out of the pictures. | How long will the repair take? | Timing varies with the damage and access needed. An accessible door ding can require much less time than a complex crease or multiple hail dents. Our technicians will discuss the expected repair time when they assess your vehicle. | Can PDR damage the paint? | PDR is intended to preserve the existing finish. Weakened paint, previous refinishing and sharp or deep damage can increase the risk of cracking or lifting. Our technicians check the area and discuss relevant limitations before work begins. | Do you repair hail damage and larger dents? | Yes, subject to assessment. Hail dents, larger dents and creases may qualify for PDR. Metal stretching, paint condition and panel access influence what can be achieved. Photos help our technicians decide the next step. | What if the dent also has a scratch? | A dent repair does not automatically repair damaged paint. Light surface marks and paint transfer are different from scratches through the finish. Our technicians can inspect the area and explain whether the dent is suitable for PDR or whether paintwork or another service is needed. | Can you work with an insurance claim? | Yes, please let us know if you plan to use insurance.
